title: Quarantine, Hold Status, Testing Context & Controlled Release

content.overview: Specialist instruction for quarantine, hold status, testing context & controlled release in propagation and clean-stock operations.

sections.title: Hold status preserves uncertainty
sections.body: Suspect material should be kept from routine downstream movement while identity, symptoms, test status or exposure history are resolved. A hold is a control state, not a diagnosis.

sections.title: Test results need context
sections.body: A test result belongs with sample identity, date, tissue/sample context, method and laboratory or procedure record. A single negative result should not be described as a permanent guarantee of clean stock.

sections.title: Release requires authority and defined evidence
sections.body: Returning held material to normal flow is a controlled decision. The course teaches what evidence should be preserved and when to escalate; it does not grant authority to release, destroy or dispose of stock.

commonMistakes: Treating quarantine as proof that material is infected.
Treating one negative test as permanent clean-stock certification.
Releasing held material because production needs it before the release decision is documented.
content.practicalApplication: Review a suspect-stock scenario and produce a status record that separates observation, exposure history, test information, hold controls, decision authority and unresolved follow-up.
content.summary: Quarantine and hold states manage uncertainty while evidence and authorized decisions are developed.
